newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid airport cracks down on slot overbooking.
newsitem.headline: Madrid airport cracks down on slot overbooking.

text.p: The Spanish airports authority AENA has cracked down on airlines for requesting extra take-off and landing slots in a bid to alleviate delays at Madrid's Barajas airport, AENA said.
The situation has deteriorated to the extent that an average of 50 percent of flights to and from Barajas suffered delays in November.

AENA has now warned it will not authorise slot requests if they do not coincide with a programmed flight time and told airlines they have to seek clearance in Madrid first instead of sending their requests directly to European controllers in Brussels.

AENA said the congestion and delays were aggravated by airlines requesting slots they then did not use and overloading the airport's capacity. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
